James A. Garfield, twentieth President of the United States, was shot on
4 July 1881 at the Baltimore and Potomac Railroad Station in Washington,
D.C. He died of his wounds on 19 September 1881 at Elberon, New Jersey.
Charles J. Guiteau was convicted of the killing and executed in 1882.

Summary of the case of President Garfield. The patient survived eighty
days after being shot on 2 July 1881. Death occurred on 19 September
1881. Infection following repeated probing of the wound is generally
held to have been the proximate cause.
